3 POWERFUL WAYS TO INVITE THE VIRGIN MARY INTO YOUR LIFE — FULTON SHEEN

How can Catholics deepen their devotion to the Blessed Virgin Mary and grow closer to Jesus Christ? This powerful Catholic message explores three meaningful ways to welcome Marian devotion into your daily life through prayer, the Holy Rosary, faith, and a deeper relationship with God.

Drawing on timeless spiritual wisdom associated with Fulton J. Sheen, this reflection explores the role of the Virgin Mary in Catholic faith, the importance of the Hail Mary and Rosary, and how sincere Marian devotion can lead the heart toward Christ.

WHAT YOU WILL DISCOVER:

• 3 powerful ways to deepen Marian devotion  
• How the Holy Rosary can strengthen your prayer life  
• Why the Hail Mary points us toward Jesus  
• How Mary’s example teaches faith, humility, and obedience  
• How Catholic devotion to Mary can deepen your relationship with Christ  

🙏 Invite Mary into your prayer life, meditate on the mysteries of Christ, and ask God for the grace to follow Jesus with greater faith and humility.

Subscribe to THE HIDDEN GOSPEL for Catholic teachings, Holy Rosary prayers, Bible wisdom, Christian spirituality, Marian devotion, and timeless messages from Fulton J. Sheen.

transcript.text: And that is why I say to you, my friends,
and I say it without apology, without hesitation,
without softening the truth for the sake of making you comfortable,
that the fastest way to the heart of Jesus Christ is through the heart of his mother.
And if you have not yet invited her into your life,
then you have been living as a spiritual orphan.
And no orphan, no matter how brave,
no matter how clever,
no matter how many good works he piles up,
can fight the battles you are fighting alone.
Because, you see, the devil is not afraid of your strength,
he is not afraid of your intelligence.
He is not even afraid of your religion,
but he trembles before the woman whose heel is destined to crush his head.
And that is not my opinion,
that is Genesis chapter 3, verse 15,
where God himself said to the serpent,
I will put enmities between thee and the woman,
and thy seed and her seed, she shall crush thy head.
And so from the very first pages of scripture,
before there was a temple,
before there was a commandment,
before there was a chosen people,
there was a promise of a woman, and that woman is Mary.
And she is not a decoration on the edges of the gospel,
she is the hinge upon which salvation turns.
And if you miss her,
you miss the way God himself chose to come into the world,
because he did not come in fire,
he did not come in earthquake, he did not come in a whirlwind.
He came as a tiny child in the womb of a woman who said yes.
And that yes,
my friends, is the door through which every grace has entered human history,
and it is the door through which every grace must enter your life as well.
Now, I am going to give you three powerful ways to invite the Virgin Mary into your life,
and I want you to listen with the ears of your soul,
not just the ears of your head,
because these are not suggestions,
these are not pious extras for people who like that sort of thing,
these are the very bones of Christian living.
And the first way is the way of the angel,
the way of the fiat,
the way of a total and complete surrender.
And I know what you are thinking.
You are thinking,
I have already given my life to God,
I have already been baptized,
I have already gone to confession,
I have already tried to be good.
But I ask you,
have you ever given yourself to Mary,
not as a stranger,
not as a distant queen,
but as a son, as a daughter,
as a child who climbs into the lap of its mother and says,
I am yours, do with me what you will.
Because that is what she did,
and that is what you must do.
And you find it in Luke chapter 1, verse 38,
where she said,
Behold the handmaid of the Lord,
be it done to me according to thy word.
And in that moment,
my friends, the universe held its breath,
because a woman's yes undid the no of Eve,
and a woman's obedience opened the gates that a woman's disobedience had closed.

transcript.text: But because she asked, and when the mother asks, the son always says yes.
And that is the first way, and it is the foundation of everything else.
Because without surrender, there is no intimacy, and without intimacy, there is no transformation.
And without transformation, you will remain exactly where you are.
A good person perhaps, a religious person perhaps, but not a saint.
And God did not create you to be merely good, he created you to be a saint.
And the quickest way to sanctity is to give yourself entirely to one who is full of grace.
Now, the second way to invite her into your life is the way of the home.
The way of Bethany, the way of Mary and Martha.
And this is a way that so many of you have forgotten.
You have forgotten that your home is meant to be a little Nazareth.
A place where heaven touches earth, a place where angels come and go.
A place where the presence of God is as real as the table you eat at.
And my friends, I want you to look at your home, really look at it, and ask yourself,
is this a place where Mary would feel welcome?
Is this a place where she would sit down and stay?
Or is it a place where the noise of the world has drowned out her voice?
And I know, I know that life is busy, I know that the kids are screaming.
I know that the bills are piling up, I know that the television is always on.
I know that the phone never stops buzzing.
But that is precisely why you need her, because she is the one who can bring silence to the storm.
She is the one who can calm the chaos, and the way you invite her into your home is by making her a living,
breathing part of it.
Not a statue that sits on a shelf gathering dust, but a presence that is felt in every room.
In every conversation, in every moment of the day.
So you begin with the rosary, my friends, and I know that for many of you the rosary is a chore.
It is a bundle of beads that you drag through your fingers while your mind wanders to a million other places.
But I want you to understand something, the rosary is not a chore.
The rosary is a conversation.
It is a walk through the life of Jesus and Mary.
It is a meditation on the mysteries of love.
And when you pray the rosary, you are not just repeating words.
You are entering into the life of the Holy Family.
You are standing in the stable at Bethlehem, you are fleeing with them into Egypt.
You are watching Jesus grow in wisdom and grace.
You are standing at the foot of the cross, and you are rejoicing at the empty tomb.
And when you pray the rosary with your family, when you gather in the living room after dinner with the lights low,
and you begin those ancient words, Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
You are inviting her into your home, and she comes.
She comes with her son, and they sit with you, and they listen to your prayers.
And they see your tears, and they know your fears, and they bring peace to that home.
A peace that the world cannot give, and the world cannot take away.
And then you make room for her, my friends, you make a little corner of your home, a little shrine.
It does not need to be grand, it does not need to cost a lot of money.
A candle, a picture, a rosary, a crucifix, anything that says, this is a place where heaven has touched this house.
And you gather there, you gather as a family, and you pray.
And you let her be the mother of your home.
You let her be the one who teaches your children, because she is the greatest teacher who ever lived.
She is the one who taught the word made flesh how to speak.
She is the one who taught the son of God how to walk.
And if she could teach him, she can teach you, and she can teach your children, and she can teach your husband,
and she can teach your wife, and she can teach you how to love.
Because she is love, she is the perfect model of love.
And when you make your home a place of prayer, when you make it a place where the rosary is prayed,
where the name of Jesus is spoken with reverence, where the saints are honored, and where the mother of God is welcomed,
you have built a fortress that no demon can penetrate.
You have built a sanctuary that the storms of life cannot destroy.
And then there is the third way, my friends, and this is the way that is most powerful, and yet most neglected.

transcript.text: suffered more than any woman who ever lived.
She suffered when she watched her son be mocked, and scourged, and crowned with thorns, and nailed to a cross.
She suffered when she held his lifeless body in her arms.
She suffered a sword piercing her own soul, just as Simeon had prophesied in the temple.
And yet she did not despair.
She did not curse God.
She did not turn away.
She stood there at the foot of the cross, and she offered it all.
She offered her suffering, united with his suffering for the salvation of the world.
And that, my friends, that is what you are called to do.
You are called to take the cross you have been given.
Whatever it is, the sickness, the loneliness, the financial hardship, the broken marriage, the rebellious child, the addiction that will not let go.
And you are called to unite it to the cross of Christ through the hands of Mary.
And when you do that, something extraordinary happens.
Your suffering is no longer meaningless.
Your suffering becomes redemptive.
Your suffering becomes a prayer.
And you become a co-redeemer with Christ, just as she was.
And there is no greater power in the universe than a soul that suffers with Mary, because that soul is participating in the very work of salvation.
And the devil cannot touch it, because the devil cannot defeat the cross, and the devil cannot defeat the woman who stood beneath it.
So go to her, my friends.
Go to her with your pain, go to her with your wounds, go to her with your failures.
And do not be afraid, because she is not a judge, she is a mother.
And a mother's heart is full of pity for the erring and the sinner, and the fallen.
And she will not turn you away, she will not scold you.
She will not remind you of all the times you have failed.
She will simply take your hand, and she will lead you to her son, and her son will forgive you, because he cannot refuse her.
And when you have been forgiven, when you have been healed, when you have been restored, she will teach you how to live.
She will teach you how to pray.
She will teach you how to love.
And she will never leave your side.
She will be with you in every trial.
She will be with you in every joy.
She will be with you in every sorrow.
And when your last hour comes, and the darkness closes in, and the enemy comes to claim you, she will be there.
And she will say, "This one is mine, this one belongs to my son."
And the enemy will flee, because he is powerless before her.
And she will take your soul, and she will present it to her son.
And her son will look at you, and he will say, "Well done, good and faithful servant.
Enter into the joy of your Lord."
And then you will see her face, and you will understand finally what it means to be loved.
And you will thank her for all eternity, for never giving up on you, for never leaving you, for always, always bringing you closer to her son.
And that, my friends, is the promise, that is the hope, that is the glory that awaits every soul that says yes to Mary.
And I beg you, do not wait another day, do not put it off another hour.
Give yourself to her now, and let her lead you home.
And when you have done that, when you have taken your cross and placed it in her hands, you will begin to see something you have never seen before.
Something I must now tell you, because it is the secret of every saint, and it is the secret that the world has tried to bury.
And it is this, and it is this, my friends, and I want you to hold on to it, because everything I have told you up to this moment has been preparation for what I am about to say.

And what I am about to say is the reason so many souls who love God still live in poverty, still live in weakness, still live in fear, still live in a kind of spiritual winter, where nothing grows and nothing blooms and nothing bears fruit.

transcript.text: And there is still more, my friends, because there is a fourth dimension to this.
And it is the one I want to press into your hands tonight like a treasure.
And that is the offering of your day, the morning oblation.
Because most of you, when you wake up in the morning, do so without a thought for heaven.
You reach for your phone before you reach for the cross.
You think about your schedule before you think about your soul.
And then the day carries you away like a river.
And by evening, you are exhausted and empty, and you wonder where the time went.
And the reason is that you never gave the day away.
You never handed it to anyone.
You never put it under the protection of the mother.
And so it was stolen from you, piece by piece, hour by hour, by the world and the flesh and the devil.
And the remedy is so simple that it sounds almost childish.
And I do not apologize for its simplicity, because God has hidden his greatest graces in the simplest things.

So when you wake, before you do anything else, before your feet touch the floor, before your eyes open fully, make the sign of the cross and say, My mother, I give you this day, my thoughts, my words, my work, my joys, my sufferings, my meetings, my driving, my cooking, my telephone calls, my fatigue, my failures.
Take it all and offer it to your son for me.
And then say, Jesus, through Mary, I love you.
And make that the first act of your day.
And then watch what happens.
Because I tell you, the day will not be the same.
The day will be governed by a queen, and the day will be surrounded by angels.
And the day will produce fruit you will not even see until you arrive in eternity.
And then you will see it.
Then you will see the conversions that came from your hidden sacrifices.
Then you will see the souls you saved by a single moment of patience that you offered through her hands.
Then you will see the graces that fell upon your children because you asked her to cover them while they slept.
And this is how the saints lived, my friends.
They did not do extraordinary things every day.
They did ordinary things extraordinarily well.
And they did them all through Mary.
And St. Louis de Montfort told us that when we consecrate ourselves to her and act through her, our smallest actions take on a value we cannot calculate, because they are no longer simply ours.
They are hers.
And they are offered by her hands.
And the hands of the mother are the hands the Father never refuses.
And now I want to speak to you about the hour of your death.
Because no man escapes that hour, and no man knows when it comes.
And there is a tradition in the church, a tradition the saints have clung to and the dying have whispered, that those who love Mary are assisted by Mary at the moment of their passing.
And St. Alphonsus wrote that her name is the joy of the dying.

And she will speak your name, and she will show you her mantle, and she will say to the enemy, this one is mine.

And I have watched this happen, my friends. I have stood at bedsides, and I have seen faces that were contorted with fear become calm as a lake, and I have heard dying lips move without sound, and I knew what they were saying.
And I have seen a hand reach up towards something that was not in the room, and I have believed with all my heart that at that moment, the mother of God had entered.
And I tell you this so that you will prepare for that hour now, while you still have breath and strength and time. Because it is too late to make friends in the last 5 minutes.
You make them now. You make them by your fidelity, by your small sacrifices, by the daily rosary that you drag yourself through when you do not feel like praying.
By the scapular you wear against your skin as a sign that you belong to her. And every one of these little things is a seed planted for the last hour of your life.
And yet, there is one more thing...
